text:
Cutter Gauthier just scored in seven straight games, 14 goals in all, a run that put his name next to Mario Lemieux and Alexander Mogilny and tied an NHL mark old enough, as Fox News put it, to have been set by guys named "Punch" and "Phantom Joe." Anaheim moved him onto the top power play (he's on for 88% of its man-advantage time, up from 55%) and he's taken it from there: 16 goals in 18 games, 14 points with the extra man.

Our numbers call it earned and lucky at once. Earned, because his chances are up: 1.76 expected goals per 60, from 1.36 last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking already had him at 99th percentile among forwards for chances from the home-plate area. Lucky, because he's shooting 20% and has 16 goals on 9.7 expected, and that rate rarely lasts.

The worry is five on five. Anaheim gets only 43.5% of the expected goals when he's out there. At 22, the shot is a weapon the Flyers will be hearing about for years. The next step is driving even-strength play, not just finishing it.
headline: Fourteen goals in seven games
